scenes.say: Week twelve. Measuring what matters, with Nicky Barton from Mutinex.
scenes.title: Measuring what matters
scenes.speaker: Nicky Barton

scenes.say: Last-click attribution gives the final click all the credit. It's like a group assignment where whoever hits submit gets the whole mark.

scenes.kicker: Crediting only the bottom of the funnel
scenes.say: Crediting only the bottom of the funnel starves the brand. Then privacy changes broke individual tracking. Ask every platform what it sold, and the answers add up to more than a hundred percent.

lines.text: Crediting only the last touch *starves the brand*.
Then Safari limits, GDPR and Apple’s “ask app not to track” broke individual tracking.
Ask every platform what it sold: the answers add up to *more than 100%*.

scenes.say: Marketing mix modelling reads the whole market: sales, spend, price, seasonality and competitors. It shows what drove sales, and where the next dollar should go.

steps.sub: Sales, spend, price, season, economy, competitors
What drove sales, ROI, the next dollar

scenes.say: It thinks in pictures. A café on a busy corner is your baseline. A song stuck in your head: ads keep working. And the fifth slice of pizza: diminishing returns.
Across eighty three brands, those that kept their brand muscle grew most. If you can't add budget, don't add channels.

lines.text: Brands that kept their *brand muscle* grew most.

scenes.say: The takeaway? Judgement becomes the job. Always ask: how do we know it worked?

lines.text: Always ask: *how do we know it worked?*
